scope: Read-only source-selection and conversion-fidelity audit of HydroLAKES and LakeATLAS local prepared releases. This does not assess producer scientific accuracy or rerun producer workflows.

source_pin_check.method: Compared source names, sizes, URLs or article/file identifiers, and recorded checksums across dataset records and retained source-inspection/fidelity evidence. Large source archives and data assets were not rehashed during this audit.

claims_checked: HydroLAKES v1 is the producer shoreline-polygon inventory for global lakes of at least 10 ha.
The producer lists polygon and pour-point downloads as separate layers and offers both geodatabase and shapefile formats.
HydroATLAS is described as a distinct, attribute-enriched product containing the HydroLAKES lake set.
The v1.0 technical document describes polygon and point attribute layers and producer fields/semantics.
HydroATLAS v1 includes LakeATLAS, the lake-polygon attribute product, and describes its hydro-environmental variables and relationship to HydroLAKES.
The technical documentation identifies LakeATLAS v1 as the HydroLAKES-derived lake unit enriched with HydroATLAS attributes, with variable/source documentation in the companion catalog.
The pinned LakeATLAS v1.0 source record; local acquisition code binds the article version, DOI, license, file IDs, sizes, and provider MD5 values.

assessment.summary: No GRWL-style geometry simplification or summary substitution is evident in the analytical polygon package. It converts the official HydroLAKES v1 polygon layer. The official pour-point layer is omitted, and that omission is explicit in the product scope and metadata.
concrete_followups: Keep product naming and claims scoped to HydroLAKES v1 polygons. If claiming the full HydroLAKES layer set, add the producer's separately distributed pour-point layer as a separate asset and validate it against its pinned source.
Retain the producer technical-document redistribution notice and review it for the intended transformed publication, as the dataset record already requires.

related_richer_or_companion_products.relationship: Separate official HydroLAKES source layer, not included in this polygon-only package.
Distinct derived product that uses HydroLAKES lake units and adds extensive hydro-environmental attributes; it is not the raw/native HydroLAKES polygon source and is separately audited below.

omitted_layers_or_detail.evidence: Official product page distributes pour points separately. Dataset record and release text state that this package contains polygons only and excludes the separate pour-point layer.
The producer identifies HydroATLAS as a distinct enriched product; it is not a missing field subset of the HydroLAKES polygon source. LakeATLAS is covered separately in this report.

package_scope_and_completeness.time_coverage: Static compiled product; no temporal observations are added or claimed.

analytical_asset_transforms: The r3 output is spatially ordered by a 16-bit Hilbert key of WGS84 bbox centers with Hylak_id tie-breaker.
GeoParquet 1.1 bbox covering is appended and recomputed from WKB.
Source-decoded original fields, nulls, and WKB are preserved; no reprojection, repair, simplification, deduplication, or WKB rewrite is reported.
display_only_transforms: The separate PMTiles display derivative uses projection/quantization/generalization for map display and selected attributes; the manifest points to the unchanged analytic GeoParquet asset for full field lookup.
Maximum-zoom display evidence accounts for all 1,427,688 source IDs, with no missing IDs reported. This is display ID accounting, not proof of analytic or scientific correctness.

validation_and_limitations.conversion_fidelity: Retained source-validation report says complete independent source/output reread through the same GDAL decoder, exact ID coverage, 1,427,688 rows, 31,409,136 compared cells, and per-feature typed digest/WKB binding. Spatial companion checks compare source values/nulls and per-ID WKB and independently recompute bbox values. Retained and clean candidate hashes match.

clean_rebuild.interpretation: The retained report records byte-equal raw and spatial artifacts and helper-recorded detached-checkout evidence. Because independent verification is explicitly false, this report does not assert an independently audited clean-checkout rebuild, nor a new end-to-end rebuild from the producer archive.

validation_and_limitations.scientific_validation: Not established. Reports state GEE parity was not run and source fidelity is not independent observational/scientific accuracy validation.
known_validation_limits: Same GDAL decoder is used for conversion and source reread; validation establishes decoded-source fidelity, not equivalence to raw DBF text encodings or independent decoding.

The polygon and pour-point layers, all decoded source fields, and source-decoded geometry are represented. No lower-detail summary substituted for the source vectors was found.
concrete_followups: Keep the OpenFileGDB warning and same-decoder limitation attached to source-fidelity claims; do not describe byte parity as raw FileGDB ring-record parity or scientific validation.

authoritative_product.relationship_to_hydrolakes: LakeATLAS uses HydroLAKES lake polygons as its spatial units and adds many hydro-environmental attributes, including information derived from external datasets and a surrounding lake-vicinity buffer. It is a distinct derived scientific data product; auditing its conversion does not mean rebuilding those producer derivations from every upstream observation/model input.

package_scope_and_completeness.field_note: The counts above are the field counts recorded by the builder/source inspection; the native OBJECTID is retained separately as the feature ID. The source inspection inventory contains both expected layers and the builder rejects an unexpected layer inventory.

analytical_asset_transforms: Both complete layer tables are streamed from the pinned File Geodatabase through GDAL/OpenFileGDB into GeoParquet.

Native identifiers and all decoded source columns/nulls are retained. The final candidate uses deterministic spatial order with OBJECTID as tie-breaker and appends bbox covering recomputed from unchanged source-decoded WKB.
No geometry repair, simplification, reprojection, or deduplication is reported.
conversion_and_display.decoder_caveat: GDAL/OpenFileGDB applies its default organizePolygons() ring classification. One polygon with more than 100 parts emits a warning. The resulting decoded WKB is retained; validation compares against the same native-layer decoder, so it does not prove identity to raw FileGDB ring-record encoding.
display_only_transforms: The separate PMTiles polygon and point layers project, quantize, and simplify geometries for display; they carry selected display attributes and source IDs.
Display manifests report all 1,427,688 source IDs accounted at maximum zoom for each layer. The complete analytical attributes and geometries remain in GeoParquet.

validation_and_limitations.conversion_fidelity: Source-fidelity evidence reports exact source-order column-array equality for all rows in both layers, then source-order reconstruction, source values/nulls/WKB comparison, and recomputed bbox checks for both spatial assets. Primary and clean spatial outputs are byte-identical. Package evidence also records STAC Node, Portolan, integrity, bounded HTTP/CORS, DuckDB subset, and final package verification passes.

clean_rebuild.interpretation: The record reports exact raw and spatial asset hash equality and helper-recorded detached-checkout evidence. The explicit false flag means the evidence should not be elevated to an independently verified clean-checkout claim. It is not an assertion that the producer's entire science pipeline was rebuilt from original observations.

validation_and_limitations.scientific_validation: Not established by conversion fidelity, package checks, or display checks. This audit found no independent scientific accuracy validation or reconstruction of all producer models and original input datasets.
known_validation_limits: Source reads for conversion and fidelity use GDAL/OpenFileGDB; raw FileGDB ring-record identity is not tested.
Same-decoder parity cannot independently establish producer scientific correctness.
Attribute observation years vary by upstream variable; the package preserves the v1 product's values and does not make them contemporaneous.

audit_commands: Read-only inspection of criteria.json, dataset.yaml files, README/VALIDATION documents, converter/source code, release manifests, source-fidelity and clean-rebuild reports, display manifests, and retained failure reports.
Python JSON reads compared source pins, reported product layers, release statuses, and clean_checkout_independently_verified flags.
Python hashlib SHA-256 was run on the small tracked text/JSON evidence files listed in evidence_inventory; no bulk source archive or analytic asset was read for hashing.
audit_result: HydroLAKES uses its authoritative full polygon layer but intentionally omits the separately published pour-point layer; this is disclosed and should remain in scope language. LakeATLAS uses the authoritative enriched v1 File Geodatabase and includes both expected polygon and point layers. Neither audit found a GRWL-like substitution of a simplified summary for the analytical vector source. Both datasets preserve conversion-fidelity evidence while explicitly lacking independent scientific validation; both clean-rebuild records explicitly set clean_checkout_independently_verified to false.
evidence_method: Evidence hashes refer to files at this Git revision; canonical records may be updated by this audit follow-up.

parent_review_of_rebuild_flag.finding: The normalizer writes clean_checkout_independently_verified=false unconditionally (bind_fidelity.py line351). Matching rebuilt asset hashes and saved clean-checkout observations are present. This flag is a conservative normalizer limitation, not evidence of a failed rebuild; it does not independently re-establish the saved checkout provenance.
